prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your exact location, system type, budget, and whether it’s an emergency. I can help you pick the best local contractor. First, a couple quick questions:

- What ZIP code or neighborhood in Phoenix are you in?
- Is this a residential or commercial system?
- Is it an emergency (no cooling right now) or routine repair/maintenance?
- Do you know the make/model/age of your AC?

While you answer, here are practical steps and criteria to quickly find a reliable HVAC company plus a phone script you can use.

How to choose (priorities)
- License & insurance: Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) license and general liability insurance. Ask for license number and verify it.
- Technician qualifications: NATE-certified techs, factory training for your brand.
- Local reviews & reputation: Google/Yelp ratings (look for many recent reviews), BBB rating, and references.
- Transparent pricing & written estimate: diagnostic fee, labor rate, flat-fee options, and written scope with parts/labor warranty.
- Warranties: parts and labor warranty terms and length.
- Emergency service & response time: 24/7 availability if you need it now.
- Permitting & code compliance: they should handle permits for replacements.
- Clean and safe work practices: COVID/respirator use, how they protect your home.
- Maintenance plans: if you want ongoing HVAC tune-ups and priority service.

Red flags
- No ROC license or won’t provide it.
- Very lowball estimates over the phone with a large “change” on-site.
- High-pressure sales for full system replacements without proper diagnostics.
- No written estimate or warranty.
- Mostly one-star reviews or recent pattern of complaints.

What to ask when you call (quick checklist)
1. Do you have an Arizona ROC license? What’s the number?  
2. Are your technicians NATE-certified or manufacturer-trained for my unit?  
3. What is your diagnostic fee and is it waived if I hire you?  
4. Do you give a written estimate before work begins?  
5. What are your parts and labor warranties?  
6. Can you provide references or recent local reviews?  
7. Are you available for emergency service and what is the response time?  
8. Do you handle permits for replacement jobs?  
9. Do you offer financing or maintenance agreements?

Sample phone script
“Hi, my name is [Name]. I’m at [ZIP] and my AC [describe problem: not cooling/short cycling/leaking]. Can you confirm your ROC license number and whether your techs are NATE-certified? What is your diagnostic fee and do you provide a written estimate before starting work? Also, what warranties do you offer?”

If you want, I can:
- Suggest 3–5 Phoenix-area HVAC companies to call (if you share your ZIP code). I can’t browse the web right now, but I’ll recommend well-known, reliably reviewed local options if you give location details.
- Draft a message/email to send to companies asking for quotes.
- Help evaluate any written estimates you receive.

Which would you like me to do next?
